## Introduction
SimLev is an R package for simulating portfolio investment strategies. This vignette will guide you through the basic usage of the package.

## Installation

```{r eval=FALSE}
# From GitHub
devtools::install_github("chemicalstats/SimLev", subdir = "r")
```

## Basic Usage

### Step 1: Prepare Market Data

SimLev requires a data.frame with at least a `date` column and price columns for each asset:

```{r}
library(SimLev)

# Create sample market data
set.seed(123)
n_days <- 365 * 5 # 5 years

data <- data.frame(
  date = seq.Date(as.Date("2018-01-01"), by = "day", length.out = n_days),
  SPY = 250 * cumprod(1 + rnorm(n_days, 0.0004, 0.012)),
  BND = 80 * cumprod(1 + rnorm(n_days, 0.0001, 0.004))
)

head(data)
```

### Step 2: Define Your Strategy

A strategy is a named list where each element defines an asset:

```{r}
strategy <- list(
  SPY = list(
    asset_class = "etf",       # ETF, ETN, ETC, or certificate
    action_type = "bnh",       # Buy-and-Hold
    asset_share = 0.60,        # 60% target weight
    asset_spread = 0.10,       # 0.10% bid-ask spread
    asset_bonus = 30,        # 30% partial exemption (German ETF rule)
    signal_buy = NULL,
    signal_sell = NULL
  ),
  BND = list(
    asset_class = "etf",
    action_type = "bnh",
    asset_share = 0.40,        # 40% target weight
    asset_spread = 0.05,
    asset_bonus = 30,
    signal_buy = NULL,
    signal_sell = NULL
  )
)
```

### Step 3: Run the Simulation

```{r}
result <- simulation(
  data = data,
  strategy = strategy,
  start_value = 10000
)

print(result)
```

### Step 4: Visualize Results

```{r}
plot(result)
```

## Adding Dollar-Cost Averaging

DCA allows you to invest a fixed amount at regular intervals:

```{r}
result_dca <- simulation(
  data = data,
  strategy = strategy,
  start_value = 10000,
  dca_mode = TRUE,
  dca_value = 500,        # $500 per month
  dca_span = 1,           # Every 1 month
  dca_unit = "month",
  dca_days = 1,           # On the 1st of each month
  dca_anchor = "start"
)

print(result_dca)
```

## Adding Rebalancing

Periodic rebalancing keeps your portfolio aligned with target weights:

```{r}
result_rebal <- simulation(
  data = data,
  strategy = strategy,
  start_value = 10000,
  balance_mode = TRUE,
  balance_span = 1,       # Every quarter
  balance_unit = "quarter",
  balance_days = 1,
  balance_thresh = 0.05   # Only if >5% deviation
)

print(result_rebal)
```

## Tax Calculation

For German investors, SimLev supports realistic tax modeling:

```{r}
result_tax <- simulation(
  data = data,
  strategy = strategy,
  start_value = 10000,
  tax_mode = "person",    # Personal taxation
  tax_rate = 26.375,     # 25% + 5.5% Soli
  liquidate = TRUE        # Sell all at end (to see tax impact)
)

print(result_tax)
```

## Complete Example

Here's a complete example combining all features:

```{r}
result_full <- simulation(
  data = data,
  strategy = strategy,
  start_value = 10000,
  # DCA
  dca_mode = TRUE,
  dca_value = 500,
  dca_span = 1,
  dca_unit = "month",
  dca_days = 1,
  balance_dca = TRUE,    # Invest in underweight assets
  # Rebalancing
  balance_mode = TRUE,
  balance_span = 1,
  balance_unit = "year",
  balance_days = 1,
  # Taxes
  tax_mode = "person",
  tax_rate = 26.375,
  # End
  liquidate = TRUE
)

summary(result_full)
```

## Comparing Strategies

```{r}
# Calculate final values
final_values <- c(
  "Lump Sum" = tail(result$worth, 1),
  "With DCA" = tail(result_dca$worth, 1),
  "With Rebalancing" = tail(result_rebal$worth, 1),
  "With Tax" = tail(result_tax$worth, 1),
  "Full Strategy" = tail(result_full$worth, 1)
)

barplot(
  final_values,
  main = "Final Portfolio Values",
  ylab = "Value ($)",
  col = "steelblue",
  las = 2
)
```
